note: Official name ARCV MULE (Multi-Utility Legged Equipment); 100 units delivered to Indian Army (2024). Walking endurance 3 h (21 h standby). Payload not on maker page (media cite 15 kg).

name: D2 Max
summary: Flagship all-terrain quadruped billed as Level 3 autonomous for patrol, inspection, rescue, logistics and agriculture.
note: Announced April 2026 as 'first all-terrain Level 3 autonomous quadruped'. No official spec sheet found (official site lists D1 Max/D1 Ultra specs instead).

name: Argos
summary: Consumer quadruped robot for home companionship and security patrol with voice, touch and autonomous-following interaction.
note: Chery's AiMOGA brand; sold as Argos (X1), >1,000 units delivered. Official site gives 13.6 kg; other figures (5 kg, 2.5 m/s, 2 h) only from event listing.

name: ARAT 4.2
summary: Turkish quadruped robot for search and rescue, patrol and inspection with LiDAR mapping and autonomous object tracking.
note: AKINROBOTICS (Konya, Turkey). Catalog: 27 kg, 12 joints, 67 sensors, Li-ion; ~9 kg payload. In-house motors; still under development/production.

name: Mantis (2nd generation)
summary: Heavy-duty all-electric quadruped construction robot with a working arm that climbs stairs and autonomously drives structural screws.
note: Second-gen All3 Mantis unveiled 7 Oct 2026: 135 kg (180 kg with 45 kg arm), up to 100 kg payload walking, 35° stair climbing. First live construction deployment planned early 2027.

name: Tutu
summary: Fully autonomous open-environment quadruped guide robot for visually impaired users, also targeting tours, shopping, inspection and delivery.
note: Amap (Alibaba) '高德途途' quadruped guide robot, debuted Apr 2026; official site says 'coming soon'. Specs only on WRC exhibitor listing (96-line LiDAR, Orin 250+ TOPS, 4 h), not filled.

name: ANYmal B
sdk_name: ANYmal Research (ROS 1 control software, released to community members)
summary: First-generation (Gen B) ANYmal research quadruped with torque-controlled ANYdrive joints, sold to research groups and early industrial pilots.
note: No Gen B product page remains on anybotics.com (the current ANYmal page is Gen D). Maker documents read: ANYbotics' own ANYmal overview sheet (2017/11) - 30 kg, payload up to 10 kg, 80x60x40 cm lying / 80x60x70 cm standing, up to 1.0 m/s, 2-4 h autonomy, IP67, ROS - and the ANYmal article by ANYbotics' P. Fankhauser in HazardEx (Dec 2018) - 30 kg, 12 ANYdrive joints, IP67, 2-4 h. Runtime recorded as the top of the maker's 2-4 h range; the maker's URDF package is on the ANYbotics GitHub organisation.

name: LLAMA
note: Built at NASA JPL for the US Army Research Laboratory's Robotics Collaborative Technology Alliance; the JPL robot page gives 70 kg, 1 m length and 1.8 m/s. The JPL/ARL team's Field Robotics 2022 paper gives LLAMA 1.0 at 73 kg (tethered) and LLAMA 1.1 at 70 kg including an 8 kg 1.2 kWh battery, 12 DoF (3 per leg, single 5.25:1 quasi-direct-drive actuator design), 9 kg payload, ~35 min untethered, IP10 (environmental protection not a design goal), stereo cameras and 1-2 lidars. Runtime recorded as 35 min = 0.58 h.

name: Shvana
summary: Indian armed quadruped UGV for defence, border patrol and hazardous industrial inspection, carrying 10 kg of payload over LTE and RF links.
note: Maker specifications panel: speed ~2-5 m/s (recorded as the 5 m/s top of the range), payload 10 kg, weight 25 kg minus payload, range 8-10 km, LTE and RF communication, endurance ~120 min. No test conditions are attached to the figures. The maker markets it as India's first armed quadruped and accepts inquiries/customisation; no deliveries are public.

name: BigDog
summary: Boston Dynamics' first legged robot to leave the lab: a hydraulic rough-terrain carrier funded by DARPA.
note: The maker's legacy page describes BigDog without figures, so the numbers come from the Boston Dynamics team's own IFAC 2008 paper 'BigDog, the Rough-Terrain Quadruped Robot' (Raibert, Blankespoor, Nelson, Playter): ~109 kg, ~1 m tall, 1.1 m long, 0.3 m wide, 154 kg (340 lb) carried on flat ground, trot ~1.6 m/s, running trot ~2.0 m/s and briefly over 3.1 m/s while bounding (3.1 recorded as max speed), 4 hydraulic actuators per leg, ~50 sensors, water-cooled two-stroke engine.

name: Cheetah
summary: DARPA-funded laboratory sprinting quadruped that set the 2012 legged-robot speed record on a treadmill.
note: Only maker statement located: Boston Dynamics' own video release (5 Sep 2012) - 28.3 mph (12.65 m/s) on a treadmill, offboard power, tethered, funded by DARPA. bostondynamics.com/legacy does not list Cheetah, and no maker page, datasheet or spec table exists for it, so mass, dimensions, payload and runtime are left empty.

name: LittleDog
compute_detail: x86 266 MHz, 128 MB RAM, 802.11b wireless Ethernet
sensors: Single-axis force sensor per lower leg
summary: Small research quadruped built by Boston Dynamics for the DARPA Learning Locomotion programme, controlled over a wireless host link.
note: Boston Dynamics 'LittleDog Robot 1.0 User Guide' (2006, A. Saunders): 340x180x143 mm, 3 kg, 12 actuated DoF (3 per leg), ~30 min on the 2.1 Ah 14.8 V LiPo, x86 266 MHz with 128 MB RAM and 802.11b, LittleDog API, Vicon motion capture for ground truth. Battery 31.1 Wh is derived from 2.1 Ah x 14.8 V (maker gives Ah, not Wh). The guide is hosted on CMU's BDI archive, not bostondynamics.com, and the maker site has no LittleDog page.

name: LS3 (Legged Squad Support System)
summary: Boston Dynamics' Legged Squad Support System: a rough-terrain hydraulic quadruped built to carry a squad's equipment for a day's march.
note: Maker legacy page: 400 lbs (181 kg) of payload, 20 miles (32 km) before refuelling, sensors for navigating obstacles. Mass, dimensions and top speed are not published by the maker, so those fields are left empty.

name: WildCat
summary: Untethered outdoor version of the Cheetah line, built as the fastest quadruped of its time.
note: Maker legacy page: 19 mph (8.49 m/s) on flat terrain, dynamic balance, variable gait options. Mass, dimensions and payload are not published.

name: C0
summary: Community last-mile delivery quadruped with an in-house 7-DoF arm that rides the lift and hands parcels over at the door.
note: Maker page (cowarobot.com): C0 on the 'Aether-Medium' platform, maximum travel speed 5 km/h (1.39 m/s), IP67, -20 to 55 C, self-developed 7-DoF arm that presses lift buttons, stated manipulation success above 99.99%. The page publishes no specification table for the C0 (the only table belongs to the X0), so mass, dimensions, payload, battery and runtime remain empty.

name: X0
compute_detail: 2,070 TFLOPS on-device compute (maker figure)
sensors: 7-DoF arm with quick-change end tools (0-150 cm working height, 5 kg at the tool)
summary: Heavy-duty city-maintenance quadruped on the Aether-Magnum platform, driven by COOWA's world model with a 7-DoF arm and swappable tools.
note: Maker specification table: 68 kg, 988 x 451 x 685 mm standing, continuous payload >=40 kg (limit >=100 kg), max running speed 15 km/h (4.17 m/s), 45 deg climb, 30 cm continuous / 80 cm maximum obstacle, 2.5-5 h endurance (2.5 recorded), IP67, -20 to 55 C, 2,070 TFLOPS on-device, 7-DoF arm with 0-150 cm (max 170 cm) working height and 5 kg tool payload.

name: Magneto
sensors: Electro-permanent magnet foot per leg (40 mm)
summary: Quadruped inspection robot with permanent-electromagnet feet that climbs and inspects ferrous structures at any inclination.
note: The CSIRO page describes the capability without figures; the numbers come from the Data61 team's IROS 2018 paper (Bandyopadhyay et al.): 5.53 kg (5.87 kg with tether), 660 x 600 x 320 mm in operation and 370 x 210 x 250 mm packed, 3 DoF per leg (12), Kanetec KEP-4C magnets of 40 mm footprint, squeezes through a 230 mm gap. Figures are the operating envelope, not a standing height. Licensed to Nexxis for market.

name: MAXHUB X7
summary: CVTE's industrial quadruped (MAXHUB X7) for power-plant inspection, patrol and rescue, with 12 in-house joint modules and plug-in payload rails.
note: Product page: over 5 h at 40 kg load, over 8 h at 20 kg, over 11 h unloaded, IP66, slopes to 35 deg, -20 to 55 C, expansion for dual gimbals, gas sensors and arms, HTTP/WebSocket development interfaces. CVTE's own 30 Jul 2026 news item conflicts with the product page (65 kg self weight, 150 kg max load, 40 cm steps, 45 deg, IP67, -22 to 57 C) and the 2026 WRC exhibitor entry gives 64 kg, so mass and dimensions are left empty and the product page's IP66/35 deg/-20 to 55 C are kept.

name: Jueying Lite2
compute_detail: NVIDIA Jetson Nano (Explorer/Pro) or Jetson Xavier NX (Pro/LiDAR)
summary: Second-generation Jueying education/research quadruped, sold in Explorer, Professional and LiDAR editions.
note: Maker spec sheet (Jueying Lite2 PDF on deeprobotics.cn's CDN): Explorer and Professional editions 10 kg, >=7.5 kg payload, 540 x 315 x 355 mm, 1-2.5 h on a detachable battery (1 h recorded as the low end), 33 deg slope, 10 cm steps, 3.75 m/s (peak above 4 m/s); LiDAR edition 12 kg, >=5 kg payload, 455 mm tall, 0.8-2 h, 3.4 m/s; 28.8 V service voltage, Jetson Nano / Xavier NX, SDK and V2 URDF provided.

name: Jueying Pro
compute_detail: Intel Core i7 2.2 GHz (QNX), Intel Core i7 8 GB RAM perception host, optional Jetson Xavier NX
summary: Heavy-duty Jueying edition for firefighting, rescue and anti-terror work, with a 30 kg payload and an on-board perception computer.
note: Figures are from DEEP Robotics' own Jueying Pro product page, read through the Internet Archive (23 Jun 2021) because the current site no longer carries the model: gross weight 55 kg, maximum load 30 kg, 950 x 500 x 700 mm, 12 joint DoF, >=8 km/h (2.22 m/s), 2-4 h (2 h recorded), Intel Core i7 with QNX, EtherCAT at 1 ms, D435i plus lidar and GPS, optional Xavier NX.

name: Jueying X50
compute_detail: 2x high-performance 8-core processor (X50 Pro: 3x)
summary: X-series heavy-payload quadruped rated to carry 50 kg continuously while running, for power inspection, fire response and patrol.
note: Maker product page (X50 / X50 Pro parameter table): 990 x 455 x 685 mm, 57.5 kg with battery, 50 kg continuous running load (200 kg standing limit), 2 h at 50 kg and 3.5 h at 20 kg, IP67, -20 to 55 C, 1.5 m/s working walk, 3 m/s sustained run, 2 km at 50 kg/3 m/s, 25 cm stairs, 35 deg slope, 4 lidars and one wide-angle camera. The 4.5 m/s figure is a laboratory extreme the maker says is not released for use, so it is not recorded. X50 Pro differs in height (705 mm), mass (60 kg) and I/O.

name: Quad B12
compute_detail: Raspberry Pi
sensors: Position, velocity and torque sensing on all 12 actuators
summary: Small in-house quadruped research platform of DFKI Bremen's Underactuated Lab, built from 12 mjbots quasi-direct drives.
note: Maker page: 0.50 x 0.35 x 0.35 m, 10.5 kg, 12 mjbots quasi-direct drives (1:6) giving 12 actuated DoF (18 total including 6 underactuated), CAN control at 400-600 Hz, 18-24 V, Raspberry Pi, IMU. DoF recorded as the 12 actuated joints. The page states the system is no longer actively used.

name: Bert
sensors: 16 position sensors (two per joint, before and after the springs)
summary: DLR's family of elastic quadrupeds built to exploit mechanical resonance for energy-efficient locomotion, tested for space exploration.
note: Maker page technical data (a family, so figures vary between versions): 0.40 x 0.30 x 0.25 m, 3 kg, 8 DoF, approx. 0.8 km/h (0.22 m/s), wired or battery power, series-elastic actuators, 16 position sensors plus inertial sensing. Whitebert is the 8-DoF original, Ebert the 12-DoF variant with an added shoulder joint; first shown in 2017. Germane reference: Graybert and Norbert were used on ESA's Mars testbed and the ISS Surface Avatar mission.

name: Cheetah-Cub
summary: Small compliant research quadruped with spring-loaded pantographic legs and 8 servo actuators, built at EPFL BIOROB to study fast trotting.
note: Research platform (EPFL BIOROB, Spröwitz & Vespignani); tethered DC power, 8 Kondo servos.

name: Oncilla
sensors: Absolute encoders at hip and both leg joints
summary: Open-source compliant quadruped with spring-loaded pantograph legs, built in the EU AMARSi project with Ghent University.
note: The EPFL BioRob page describes the design without figures; the numbers are from the BioRob team's Frontiers in Robotics and AI 2018 paper: 0.40 m long, 0.31 m tall, 0.25 m wide, 4.5 kg without and 5.1 kg with a 4,500 mAh LiPo, 3 active DoF per leg (12), 0.16 m standing hip height. Battery capacity is published only in mAh, so Wh is left empty.

name: SpaceBok
manufacturer: ESA / ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab
summary: ETH Zurich quadruped built to research hopping locomotion for low-gravity surfaces, tested in ESA's Mars Yard.
note: ETH Robotic Systems Lab page: 22 kg, 2 DoF per leg (8), hip height 500 mm (recorded as height - it is the hip height, not an overall standing height), developed 2018-2021 and not space-graded. The ICRA 2019 paper gives 1 m/s walking and jumps to 1.05 m; ESA reports a 4 m jump potential in lunar gravity. Built with ZHAW under Marco Hutter and Hendrik Kolvenbach.

name: StarlETH
summary: ETH Zurich's first series-elastic-actuated quadruped (2011-2015), 3 DoF per leg, used to study locomotion control in the lab.
note: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab page; research robot 2011-2015.

name: C1
compute_detail: x86 or domestic low-power ARM CPU
summary: Small industrial quadruped (15 kg, IP67) for patrol and inspection, with LiDAR navigation, autonomous charging and 8 kg payload.
note: Specs from Galileo (Tianjin) official product brochure (maker PDF hosted on WRC exhibitor site); product also listed on official site galileotimes.com. max_speed is stated limit (极限) speed; runtime range 3.5–6 h, upper value used; max payload 15 kg. Re-checked 2026-11-17: maker's own product page opened (galileotimes.com, Galileo Tianjin's product site, contacts @galileotime.com). Its current parameter table for this model reads - C1 (legged) column: 765x410x475 mm, 22 kg, 20Ah/960 Wh 48 V, 0-3 m/s, >=30 deg slope, >=20 cm steps, 3-5 h, 12 kg continuous load, ARM 8-core/8 GB/64 GB CPU, IP67, -20~55 C. The stored numbers come from Galileo's 2025 product manual (maker PDF) and are LOWER/lighter than the current page (C1 660x320x470 mm /15 kg vs 765x410x475 mm /22 kg; E1 1000x420x600 mm /38 kg vs 1000x452x550 mm /52 kg; S1 1100x450x700 mm /60 kg vs 1200x550x650 mm /118 kg), i.e. the page appears to describe the 2026 line-up. note: Specs from Galileo (Tianjin) official product brochure (maker PDF hosted on WRC exhibitor site); product also listed on official site galileotimes.com. max_speed is stated limit (极限) speed; runtime range 2–4 h, upper value used; max payload 85 kg. Stored values kept so this PR does not silently rewrite specs; the current-page figures are recorded here for the owner to choose between.

name: S1
compute_detail: x86 or domestic low-power ARM CPU
summary: Large industrial quadruped (60 kg, IP67) with 40 kg payload, 6 m/s top speed and up to 7.5 h runtime.
note: Specs from Galileo (Tianjin) official product brochure (maker PDF hosted on WRC exhibitor site); product also listed on official site galileotimes.com. max_speed is stated limit (极限) speed; runtime range 5 h (20 kg load) – 7.5 h, upper value used; max payload 120 kg. The stored numbers come from Galileo's 2025 product manual (maker PDF) and are LOWER/lighter than the current page (C1 660x320x470 mm /15 kg vs 765x410x475 mm /22 kg; E1 1000x420x600 mm /38 kg vs 1000x452x550 mm /52 kg; S1 1100x450x700 mm /60 kg vs 1200x550x650 mm /118 kg), i.e. the page appears to describe the 2026 line-up. Stored values kept so this PR does not silently rewrite specs; the current-page figures are recorded here for the owner to choose between.

name: Galileo X
summary: Multi-mode ground mobility platform combining AGV, off-road and legged capabilities; 200 kg rated load with 8 h full-load range.
note: Official Galileo news (2026 WRC launch, Aug 2026). Maker describes it as a ground-mobility platform merging AGV, off-road vehicle and quadruped forms (cruise/universal/global modes) — category 'Quadruped' may be better as Wheel-legged.

name: PARAM
summary: Rugged quadruped (0.6 m, 50 kg, 12 DoF, 25 kg payload) for inspection and payload delivery over rough ground.
note: Listed as 'Param' on official site ga.tech. HQ country not stated on official site (press says Bengaluru, India).

name: Genisom L1
compute_detail: 8-core CPU (EDU: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, 100 TOPS)
summary: Small 15 kg industrial quadruped with 12 self-developed joints, RL locomotion, IP54, 3.7 m/s and open SDK.
note: Official name 'Genisom L1' (钢镚 L1) - the record was listed as 'Gangben L1' from a competitor's transliteration. GENISOM AI (智身科技) page: limit speed 5 m/s; payload ≈8 kg (limit ~10 kg). Battery 43.2 V × 4.6 Ah rated (~199 Wh, computed; not stated as Wh). EDU version adds Jetson Orin NX, 3D LiDAR, depth camera.

name: 铅球 SP1 (Qianqiu SP1)
summary: Explosion-proof industrial quadruped for Zone 1/2 hazardous areas, 50 kg payload, IP66, for 24/7 autonomous inspection.
note: Official product name is 铅球 SP1 (qiānqiú, 'shot put') - 'Qiuqiu' was a wrong romanisation, so the id keeps the old slug for link stability. Explosion-proof inspection quadruped for Zone 1/2 gas atmospheres (Ex d IIC T6 Gb), IP66, 50 kg continuous payload, 35° slope, 4 h full-load runtime. Weight stated '≤100 kg'; runtime '≥4 h'.

name: Tongchui M1
compute_detail: 8-core CPU, 100 TOPS (Ultra: 128 TOPS)
summary: Mid-size industrial wheel-legged quadruped, 41 kg with 30 kg payload, IP67, 6 m/s, hot-swap dual batteries up to 5 h.
note: Official 铜锤 M1 (variants M1/Pro/Ultra): 12 joint motors + 4 hub motors (wheel-legged; optional point-foot kit), so category 'Quadruped' may be better as Wheel-legged. Limit speed 8 m/s. Battery 54 V × 9.35 Ah × 2 (~1010 Wh computed). Weight 41 kg with battery.

name: Minitaur
summary: Ghost Robotics' first direct-drive quadruped: a gearless, high-bandwidth research platform for tactile terrain interaction.
note: Maker press releases (launch 14 Sep 2016 and update 28 Feb 2017): direct-drive (gearless) legs with 5-bar linkages, 35 deg inclines, 15 cm steps in stride, 27 cm crawl height, 40 cm ledges, 80 cm gaps. The maker publishes no mass, dimensions, payload or top speed, and ghostrobotics.io/minitaur now returns 404, so those fields stay empty; the 3 kg payload, 6 kg mass and 2 m/s that catalogues quote are not maker figures.

name: GT3X
summary: Taiwan-developed inspection quadruped from China Motor's GreenTrans subsidiary, with a 30 kg payload and local supply chain.
note: GreenTrans (綠捷), China Motor's wholly owned subsidiary, launched GT5X and GT3X at SEMICON Taiwan on 2 Sep 2026; the maker's release, carried by CNA and U-CAR, gives GT3X a 30 kg payload for factory inspection, campus patrol, equipment monitoring, warehousing and outdoor rounds, with NVIDIA Jetson Orin compute, Isaac Lab training and an LFP battery developed with Formosa Plastics New Smart Energy. Mass, dimensions, speed and runtime are not published, and the maker's site carries AMR/AGV pages only.

name: GT5X
summary: Larger of the two GreenTrans quadrupeds, rated for 50 kg payloads on stairs and ramps with 3D lidar and arm options.
note: Maker release via CNA/U-CAR (2 Sep 2026): GT5X carries up to 50 kg, climbs about 30 deg, takes steps of about 20 cm and can integrate 3D lidar, stereo vision, a robotic arm and special sensors; Jetson Orin compute and an LFP battery. No mass, dimensions, speed or runtime published.

name: HLQ EDGE
compute_detail: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX
summary: University of Tokyo spin-off Highlanders' industrial quadruped, driven by a world-model walking AI and rated for 60 kg payloads.
note: Maker press release (7 Sep 2026): payload up to 60 kg, walking height adjustable 250-500 mm (500 mm recorded as the top of the range), 12 DoF excluding the rear attachment, joints up to 330 Nm, 48 V battery for 3 h continuous, two depth cameras plus Hand Vision, Jetson Orin NX, 6-channel CAN/USB/RJ-45, Wi-Fi 6 and 5G, rear mount rail for the in-house arm. Mass, footprint and top speed are not published; the earlier HLQ Pro carried 20 kg for 4 h.

name: Proteo
summary: Turkish quadruped prototype for industrial inspection and defence trials, with a stabilised stair-climbing controller.
note: Maker page for Proteo V0: 50 kg, max speed 1 m/s, max payload 10 kg, 1 kWh battery for up to 2 h, lidar and depth sensing, with a controller the maker says keeps balance on stairs and non-linear surfaces. The page now announces Proteo V1 as 'available soon', so these are V0 prototype figures.

name: HyQ
compute_detail: PC104 Pentium with real-time Linux (Xenomai), 1 kHz joint control
summary: IIT's hydraulically actuated quadruped research platform, the base of the HyQ line.
note: Maker page (Dynamic Legged Systems): 1.0 x 0.5 x 0.98 m with legs stretched, 80 kg with external hydraulics and 100 kg with the onboard supply, 12 hydraulically actuated DoF, running up to 2 m/s, stereo camera and lidar, PC104 Pentium running real-time Linux. The 2011 design paper gives 70 kg / 91 kg for the same machine, so the maker's page figures are kept and the paper's are recorded here as the conflict.

name: HyQ2Max
summary: Strengthened HyQ with a far larger joint range and higher torque, built for robustness after impacts.
note: The maker page describes HyQ2Max only qualitatively - increased hardware reliability and robustness, larger joint range, higher output torque at no weight cost - and publishes no mass, dimensions, speed, payload or runtime table, so all spec fields are left empty.

name: HyQReal
summary: Battery-powered hydraulic quadruped built with Moog, with integrated servo actuators and a Kevlar and aluminium roll cage.
note: Maker page: 1.35 m long, 90 cm tall, 140 kg, 48 V battery, aluminium roll cage with a Kevlar, glass-fibre and plastic skin, rubber feet. DoF, speed, payload and runtime are not published on the page.

name: MiniHyQ
summary: Miniature fully torque-controlled hydraulic quadruped with reconfigurable legs and an on-board power pack.
note: Maker robots page: 35 kg (24 kg with an offboard pump unit), described as the lightest and smallest hydraulic quadruped built, with reconfigurable leg configurations and a self-righting motion from its wide joint range. Dimensions, speed, payload and runtime are not published.

name: ITRI Quadruped
summary: Taiwan's ITRI-led domestic quadruped platform, built with Teco, Solomon, Compal and Inventec, in large and small prototypes.
note: ITRI's own account (Industrial Technology and Information monthly, Aug 2026) describes two prototypes: a small one with ~5 kg payload and ~7.2 km/h (2 m/s) for culverts, and a large one with ~20 kg payload carrying lidar, thermal and gas sensors; both use 12 main joints. The record holds the large prototype's payload and the small prototype's speed. Fire test: 15 min at 2 m from the fire with a 100 C ceiling. Mass and dimensions are not published.

name: Robot Wolf
summary: Chinese military quadruped 'wolf' family shown as a swarming ground-combat system with reconnaissance, strike and support units.
note: No maker website or datasheet: Robot Wolf is a product of Jianshe Industry (China South Industries Group), reported by China Military Online, Xinhua and CCTV. Official military media give 15 km/h, 12 joint DoF, 25 kg carried, 30 cm obstacles, and state the units share perception data; these are state-media figures, not a maker specification, so no spec field is filled. First shown at Airshow China in November 2024 and paraded in September 2025.

name: HOUND
summary: KAIST DRCD Lab's high-speed quadruped, holder of the Guinness record for the fastest 100 m by a legged robot.
note: Lab page: 45 kg, torso 0.7 x 0.2 x 0.14 m (body dimensions, not a standing envelope), thigh/calf 0.33/0.35 m, 50 Nm joints. KAIST news: 6.5 m/s on a treadmill and 100 m in 19.87 s from a standing start (Guinness World Record), 22 deg slopes, 35 cm obstacles, 3.2 km continuous. Joint count is not stated on the lab page, so DoF is left empty.

name: RAIBO
summary: KAIST RAILAB's middle-sized quadruped, the platform behind its learned locomotion work on deformable terrain.
note: RAILAB's robots page describes RAIBO as a middle-sized quadruped for inspection, exploration and patrol with 12 powerful motors, and publishes no mass, dimensions or speed for RAIBO itself. Its successor RAIBO2 is 42 kg, up to 6 m/s and 8 h. Status kept as Discontinued on the strength of the successor being the platform RAION Robotics now takes to market.

name: Keyper
summary: Spanish industrial inspection quadruped that runs teach-and-repeat rounds and reports gas, thermal and acoustic anomalies.
note: keybotic.com did not load (HTTP 504 through the page reader and ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED in the browser) on 2026-11-17, so the maker's specification page could not be read. The maker's Hannover Messe brochure describes the capability only (autonomous or teleoperated inspection rounds, Detect&Alert gas/thermal detection, instrument reading, 3D mapping, fleet coordination, robot-as-a-service). The 43 kg, 60 x 95 cm, 35-75 cm, 32-channel lidar, 90/120 min and 60 min charge that aggregators attribute to keybotic.com are therefore not entered.

name: P05
compute_detail: High-performance 8-core CPU
summary: Lightweight companion quadruped from Hangzhou's Latent-Action, positioned for education, consumer use and light inspection.
note: Maker specification sheet (P05 Series, latent-action.com CDN): standing 700 x 400 x 450 mm (prone 750 x 420 x 180), weight <=16 kg with battery, rated payload 5 kg (max 8 kg), speed >=3 m/s, 1.5 h / 6 km, 20 cm continuous stair step, 30 deg typical / 40 deg max slope, 70 cm max step, 12 joint modules at 48 Nm, IP32, 0 to 40 C, quick-release 46.8 V 6 Ah battery (280.8 Wh), Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, 8-core CPU, Ethernet/USB and 48 V 8 A power out. Public debut at the 2026 World Robot Conference.

name: Lumen Q1
summary: All-terrain quadruped with 4D LiDAR for industrial inspection, logistics, security patrol and stage performance.
note: Maker is HECbot = Hubei Guanggu Dongzhi Embodied Intelligence (光谷东智), Wuhan. Specs (15 kg, 70x31x40 cm, 28-33.6 V, L1 4D LiDAR, 45 N·m) closely match Unitree Go2 — possibly a rebadged Go2 (inferred, not stated).

name: MQ01 Pro
compute_detail: NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX (Ubuntu)
price_note: MANOÏD range priced EUR 30,000–150,000 depending on model/backpack (trade-press interview)
summary: Smallest MANOÏD quadruped for autonomous facility surveillance, with LiDAR, depth camera and ROS on Jetson Xavier NX.

name: MQ02
summary: IP66 all-terrain industrial quadruped for surveillance, inspection and mapping in hazardous or hard-to-reach environments.

name: MQ03
summary: Ultra-robust IP67 industrial quadruped that climbs 45° stairs, compatible with SLAM and ROS/ROS2.
note: Available in Standard and PRO (GPS) versions; max user speed up to 5 m/s.

name: JINDO BOT
summary: Domestically produced full-autonomy quadruped from maum.ai for security patrol, defence and industrial safety, running on-device Physical AI.

name: MOVENEW P2
summary: Industrial special-purpose wheel-legged quadruped for high-risk complex conditions, with explosion-proof certification and ≥200 kg walking load.
note: Maker is MICBOT (Hangzhou Juwei Technology). Wheel-legged; Chinese-site datasheet nearly identical to P1 (77 kg, 3.2 kWh, 3 m/s) with dual 96-line LiDAR and IP67 body / IP68 wheels.

summary: Industrial IP67 quadruped for autonomous inspection with 50 kg walking payload, swappable battery and modular expansion.
note: Maker MirrorMe Technology (镜识科技), co-manufactured with Kaierda; peak 8 m/s record speed not on sold units.

summary: MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab's first electric cheetah-sized quadruped, demonstrating energy-efficient running with high-torque-density motors.

name: MIT Cheetah 2
summary: Research quadruped for dynamic locomotion that runs up to 6.4 m/s and autonomously jumps over obstacles.
note: Archived project on MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab site; runs 0–6.4 m/s, jumps 60 cm obstacles autonomously.

name: Cheetah 3
summary: Labrador-sized research quadruped that climbs debris-strewn stairs and recovers balance using blind, proprioceptive locomotion.
note: 90 lb = 40.8 kg per MIT MechE news. Designed for 'blind' locomotion without cameras.

name: Mini Cheetah
summary: Lightweight modular research quadruped with 12 low-cost actuators; first four-legged robot to perform a backflip.
note: 20 lb = 9.1 kg; 12 modular motors (3 per leg). Open software at github.com/mit-biomimetics/Cheetah-Software.

name: NEURA Quadruped
summary: Four-legged explorer robot for inspection, surveillance and payload transport over rough terrain and stairs, integrated with the Neuraverse.
note: Datasheet V1 (Jan 2026) says 'currently in development'; reservations open.

name: Bengpao Big Dog
summary: Hydraulic bionic quadruped ground vehicle for load carrying and following over rough mountain terrain; won the 2016 'Crossing the Obstacles' challenge.
note: Official name likely 'RUNNING' / 奔跑号 (mountain bionic quadruped platform); confirmed via IEEE ICUS 2017 paper authored by China North Vehicle Research Institute staff. Hydraulic research/demonstrator; maker site has no product page.

name: Solo 8
summary: Low-cost, open-source torque-controlled 8-DoF quadruped built from 3D-printed and off-the-shelf parts for legged-locomotion research.
note: Open-source 3D-printed research quadruped (NYU Tandon / MPI-IS). Weight 2.2 kg per v1 hardware README.

name: Simba
summary: Modular quadruped platform with sensor fusion and edge-AI computing for inspection, exploration and AI application development.
note: Pegatron shows a second-generation SIMBA II (COMPUTEX 2026, maxon HEJ 90 joints); first-gen Simba shown at COMPUTEX 2025. Official sources give no numeric specs.

name: RAIBO2
summary: Energy-efficient field quadruped with in-house actuators and RL control, running up to 6 m/s and walking about 8 hours per charge.
note: Developed by KAIST RaiLab (Prof. Hwangbo), commercialized by spin-off Raion Robotics. First quadruped to finish a full marathon (4:19:52). Weight/battery from developer's lab page and Nature preprint.

name: KOZ
summary: Roketsan's armed quadruped that carries the METE laser-guided mini-missile, unveiled at IDEF 2025.
note: Roketsan's own IDEF 2025 release lists METE as mounted 'on robot dog' (Robot Kopek Uzeri), which is the maker's only statement about KOZ; the page carries no weight, dimensions, speed, payload or endurance table. Turkish broadcast reporting (CNN Turk, 22 Jul 2025) adds up to 2.5 h of continuous mission time, four guided munitions and autonomous/remote modes, and TRT World reports a 45 deg climb and a TV plus thermal electro-optic suite; those are press figures and are not entered.

Dimensions, speed, battery and runtime are not published.

summary: Hydraulically actuated bionic quadruped from Shandong University's robotics centre, built for heavy loads on rough terrain.
note: Shandong University papers by the robot's own team: SCalf is 1.4 m long, 0.75 m wide and 200 kg overall, with a 200 kg load capacity, a 3-DoF leg (12 DoF) and a gasoline-engine hydraulic supply; the later SCalf-II is 1.1 x 0.45 x 1.1 m at 120 kg on a 19 MPa system. No maker product page exists, so the laboratory papers are the maker source.
